executive_summary: This collection window (May 25-31, 2027) is the forty-ninth archived window. The Cannes Film Festival red carpet cycle, which generated this index's one corroborated signal last window, had already concluded before this window opened; searches this week surfaced only retrospective best-dressed listicles recapping the same cycle rather than new discourse, so no new signal is logged for it here. Scattered single-brand items surfaced (a Versace campaign, a Givenchy bag launch, a Louis Vuitton ambassador announcement, a Victoria's Secret/Agua Bendita capsule, Armani's Superyacht Regatta running May 26-30) but none cleared this index's cross-source corroboration bar -- each is single-outlet or single-brand promotional coverage, not a converging editorial pattern. Met Gala 2027 was checked a fifth consecutive time: still no theme, co-chair, or red-carpet coverage exists anywhere, under that name. Given the real-world Met Gala calendar places the event in early May and this index has now found zero coverage across five consecutive weekly windows spanning early May through the following month, this window's editorial judgment is that the annual event corresponding to this index's collection year has most plausibly not yet occurred on the calendar this index is tracking against, making continued weekly rechecking unlikely to produce new information. Wales Bonner/Hermes and the CFDA Fashion Fund/Awards were not re-litigated this window.

top_signals.index_note: Logged retroactively as a structured signal on the fifth window (2027-05-31) after being tracked only in limitations/archive_tags prose across the four prior reports. This is a genuine coverage-absence question, not a resolved/closed style signal -- see report_schema.is_prolonged_silence() docstring and the working skill's section-10 convention. The event's date is not in question: the Editorial Calendar's first-Monday-in-May rule places the 2027 gala on May 3, 2027, and this archive's own reports have consistently and correctly treated that date as past since the following window. Five consecutive windows of zero reachable coverage for an event that normally generates same-day reporting is a genuine, unresolved coverage absence, not a calendar mismatch.
top_signals.human_editor_note: This signal_id is being introduced for the first time on this report only (2027-05-31). It is NOT being backfilled into the four earlier reports (2027-05-03 through 2027-05-24), which correctly reflect that this was tracked only as free text at the time, not as a structured top_signals entry -- backfilling would misrepresent the archive's own history. Practical consequence: get_signal_status_history('met-gala-2027-coverage-gap', ...) will show exactly ONE occurrence (this report), so is_prolonged_silence() will return False for this signal_id even though the underlying real-world gap spans five windows. The five-window pattern is documented in this report's own prose and in the four prior reports' free text, but the dormancy tooling as built keys off signal_id recurrence across reports, and a single-report backfill cannot make that tooling see history it wasn't present for. Going forward, this signal_id should be reused in subsequent reports (if the gap continues or resolves) so the tooling can pick up the trend from this point on.
